gloss: all ages; ancient and modern times

definitions.gloss: all ages; ancient and modern; throughout history
definitions.explanation: Literary noun combining {古|こ} (old) and {今|こん} (now), referring to all eras from antiquity to the present. Almost always used in fixed expressions or titles rather than as a free-standing word.

examples.japanese: {古今|ここん}{東西|とうざい}の{名作|めいさく}を{集|あつ}めた。
examples.english: We have gathered masterpieces from all times and places.

examples.japanese: {古今|ここん}{無双|むそう}の{英雄|えいゆう}と{言|い}われている。
examples.english: He is said to be a hero without equal in any age.

examples.japanese: {古今|ここん}{東西|とうざい}を{問|と}わず、{人|ひと}は{愛|あい}について{語|かた}り{続|つづ}けてきた。
examples.english: Regardless of era or culture, people have always talked about love.

notes:
Literary compound of {古|こ} (old) + {今|こん} (now). In modern Japanese it appears almost exclusively in set phrases and classical titles, not as a stand-alone noun.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {古今|ここん}{東西|とうざい}: all times and places (everywhere, in every era)
- {古今|ここん}{東西|とうざい}を{問|と}わず: regardless of time or place
- {古今|ここん}{無双|むそう}: unmatched in any era
- {古今|ここん}{和歌集|わかしゅう}: the Kokin Wakashū (10th-century poetry anthology)

REGISTER:
Formal and literary. Common in essays, speeches, and historical writing; rare in casual conversation, where {昔|むかし}から{今|いま}まで is more natural.
